newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds higher, sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds higher, sluggish trade.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late Friday, gaining support from U.S. Treasuries throughout the session.
"The market was sustained," said a trader at an Argentine bank.
Although the market gained ground, activity was sluggish, reflecting the increasing feeling that the market's January rally may be about to run out of steam.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.10 to 125.90, while the FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/4 to 89-5/8.
Another trader said: "90 on the FRB will be a key psychological level for the market to break through." The FRB hit a high of 89-7/8 this session however, just short of the 90 level.

The market put in another strong performance this week, with especially peso-denominated bonds gaining. Peso bonds gained from the issue of a 10-year 500 million peso Eurobond and a B1 rating on Argentine peso debt from Moody's rating agency.
Call money rates fell to 5.05 percent from 5.15 percent.
